questions.question: The official motto of the 36th edition of the National Games 2022 of India was ______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **36th edition of the National Games 2022** of India was **held in Gujrat** from September 29 to October 12.
 
• The **motto** of the games was **"Celebrating unity through sports"**.
 
• The Motto was chosen to promote the spirit of sportsmanship and togetherness among the participating states and union territories.

__
 
• The duration and the regulations of the National Games are entirely within the jurisdiction of the Indian Olympic Association.
 
• The 1st edition of the Indian Olympic Games held at Lahore in an undivided Punjab in 1924.
 
• The first three editions were all held in the city of Lahore.
 
• After the eighth edition in 1938 in Calcutta, the event was christened as the National Games.
 
• The city of Lucknow hosted the National Games in its first post-independence avatar.
 
• The first National Games on the lines of the Olympics were held in 1985 in New Delhi.
 
• The 37th edition was held in Goa from 25 october to 9th november 2023.
 
 
• The official mascot for the 2023 National Games of India was Moga, an Indian bison.
 
• The motto of the 37th National Games was "Get Set Goa".

questions.question: Who among the following political leaders became the chief minister of Bihar, India in August 2022?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitish Kumar** is an Indian politician who has served multiple terms as the **Chief Minister of Bihar.**
 
• He is a member of the** Janata Dal (United) party.**
 
• He has been the **22nd Chief Minister of Bihar** since **22 February 2015**, having previously held the office from 2005 to 2014 and for a short period in 2000.
 
• He is **Bihar's longest-serving chief minister.**
 
• The **Janata Dal (United)** was formed by **Nitish Kumar, George Mathew Fernandes** and **Sharad Yadav** faction of the Janata Dal, the Lok Shakti Party and the Samata Party **on 30 October 2003**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tarkishore Prasad **is an Indian politician belonging to the **Bharatiya Janata Party** who served as the **Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar from 16 November to 9 August 2022.**
 
• **Renu Devi** is an Indian politician from Bharatiya Janata Party who served as the **Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar from 16 November 2020 to 9 August 2022.**

questions.question: If loan exposure is supported by collateral, it’s said to be ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**secured credit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secured credit** is a type of loan that is **backed by collateral. **
 
• Secured credit is commonly used for **mortgages, auto loans, and secured credit cards.**
 
• Secured credit is considered **less risky for lenders** because they have a way to recover their money if the borrower defaults on the loan. This makes it **easier for borrowers** **with poor credit to get approved for a loan**.
 
• **Collateral is an asset** that the borrower **pledges as security for the loan**. 
 
 
• **Collateral **can take many forms, including **real estate, vehicles, stocks, and jewellery**. 
 
• If the borrower defaults on the loan, the lender can seize the collateral to recover the amount owed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unsecured credit** is a type of loan which are **not backed by collateral**. Lenders rely on the borrower's creditworthiness to determine if they will be able to repay the loan. Unsecured credit is considered **riskier for lenders** and therefore, typically comes with **higher interest rates.**

 
 
• **Unsecured credit** is commonly used for **credit cards, personal loans, and student loans.**
 
 
 
• **Poor credit** refers to a** low credit score or a history of missed payments and defaults**. Borrowers with poor credit may have difficulty getting approved for loans or may be **charged higher interest rates to compensate for the increased risk.**
 
• **High credit **refers to a **good credit score and a history of responsible credit management.** Borrowers with high credit are more likely to be approved for loans and may be **offered lower interest rates.**

questions.question: Statutory body of higher education, which was set up during the first five year plan in India, ______.

options.text: All India Council of Technical Education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**University Grants Commission.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **University Grants Commission (UGC)** came into existence on **28 December 1953** under **the first five-year plan in India** to promote and coordinate university education.
 
• It became** a statutory body** under **University Grants Commission Act 1956.**
 
• It is the main **regulatory body for higher education** in India.
 
• It is responsible for providing recognition to universities in India and disbursing funds to them for development and research purposes.
 
• It sets quality standards for higher education institutions in India and monitors their compliance.
 
• It also provides financial assistance to universities and colleges for the development of infrastructure and research facilities.
 
• In **2018**, UGC was **replaced by the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)** which will act as a single regulator for higher education institutions in India. However, the proposal is** yet to be implemented.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE)** was established in **1993**.

 
 
• It regulates and coordinates teacher education programs in India.
 
• It is **a statutory body** of the Indian government set up under the **National Council for Teacher Education Act of 1993.**
 
 
 
• The **Medical Council of India(MCI)** was first established in **1934** under the **Indian Medical Council Act, of 1933**.
 
 
• It was later reconstituted as **a statutory body** under the **Indian Medical Council Act, 1956** which replaced the earlier Act.
 
• It was **regulating medical education and profession** in India.
 
• It was for establishing uniform and high standards of medical education in India until its dissolution **on 25 September 2020** when it was **replaced by the National Medical Commission(NMC)**
 
 
 
• The **All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE)** was established in **1945 **as a national-level apex advisory body to conduct a survey on the facilities available for technical education and to promote development in the country in a coordinated and integrated manner.
 
 
• It is responsible for **regulating and coordinating technical education** in India.
 
• It became **a statutory body** under the **All India Council For Technical Education Act 1987**.

questions.question: The Governor of the state is appointed by the ______.

options.text: Prime minister (on the advice of the central government)
Chief Minister (on the advice of the central government)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****The Governors of states:**

__
 
• **Governors** have been discussed under** Article 153 to Article 162** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India and is responsible for the administration of the state.
 
• Under **Article 155**, the **appointment of the Governor** is done **by the President **of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• He/She holds office at the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove the Governor from office at any time without assigning any reason.
 
• The **term **of governor's office is **normally 5 years **but it can be terminated earlier.
 
• He/She can also resign from his/her office by addressing the resignation letter to the President.
 
• Under **Article 157**, the **qualifications for appointment as a Governor** are: A Governor must
 
 
• be an** Indian citizen** and reside in the country.
 
• attain an age of a **minimum of 35 years**.
 
• not be a member of both houses of the parliament and the house of the state legislature.
 
• not hold any office for generating profit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Prime Minister** of India is the head of the government at the centre.
 
• Under** Article 75**, he/she is **appointed by the president** of India if he/she has the confidence of the majority of Lok Sabha members.
 
 
• He can recommend a person's name for the post of Governor to the President.
 
• **Article 74(1) **states that there shall be a **Council of Ministers** with a** Prime Minister at the head** to aid and advise the President.
 
 
 
• ​The **Chief Minister of a state** head of the government at the state level.
 
 
• According to **Article 164** in the Indian Constitution, the **Governor appoints a Chief Minister.**

questions.question: The north-west part of India receives rainfall in winter due to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Disturbance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western Disturbances** are low-pressure systems that** originate in the Mediterranean region** and move towards the Indian subcontinent.
 
• These disturbances **bring rainfall to the north-western parts of India during **the** winter** months, and they also affect the weather conditions in other parts of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The South-west monsoon** is the **primary rainy season in India**, which** starts in** **June and lasts till September**.

 
 
• This monsoon is** caused by** the differential heating of land and sea, which results in the formation of** low-pressure systems over the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea.**
 
 
 
• **The North-east is** known as the **winter monsoon**, the northeast monsoon approaches India from the northeast.
 
 
• During this time, rainfall is common throughout the southern region of India, particularly in Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **The Retreating Monsoon**, also **known **as the **North-East monsoon,** brings** rainfall to the southern parts of India during October and November.**
 
 
• This monsoon is **caused by the withdrawal of the south-west monsoon winds** and the formation of a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: The term "Juvenile" under Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 refers to a person ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is below 18 years of age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015** was enacted to provide for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children who conflict with the law and children in need of care and protection.
 
• The Act defines a **Juvenile** as any **person who has not completed 18 years of age.** The **earlier Juvenile Justice Care and Protection of Children Act 2000** defined a juvenile as a **person below 16 years.**
 
• The term "Juvenile" is used to refer to a young person who is not yet an adult and is considered to be under the age of majority.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An important provision of the amended Act is that it provides for **minors in the age group 16 – 18 years to be treated as adults in the case of heinous crimes.**
 
• It also gives definitions for petty, serious, and heinous crimes by children.
 
 
• A **heinous offense attracts** a **maximum punishment of 7 years** imprisonment under any existing law.
 
• A **serious offense attracts** **imprisonment **of **3 to 7 years**.
 
• A** petty offense attracts** a **maximum of 3 years imprisonment.**
 
 
 
• The Act gives more clarity on the functions and powers of the **Juvenile Justice Board** and the **Child Welfare Commission.**

questions.question: Srimanta Sankardeva received recognition for which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya Dance **has its origin in the **‘Sattras’ established by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev** in the **15th and 16th centuries. **
 
• The Sattras were established for the propagation of Vaishnavism and later became the religious, cultural and social hub of Assam.
 
• The Sattriya dance can be classified into** two styles**, namely** ‘Paurashik Bhangi’ i.e. Tandava or Masculine style** and** ‘Stri Bhangi’ i.e. Lashya or feminine style.**
 
• On November 15 in the year **2000**, the **Sangeet Natak Akademi of India recognized Sattriya as one of the eight classical dances of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev **was a great** Vaishnavite saint** and reformer born in **Alipukhuri, Nagaon, Assam** in **1449**.
 
• He was a saint, scholar, playwright, social and religious reformer is a colossal figure in the cultural and religious history of Assam.
 
• **‘Ek Sarania Nam Dharma’ **preached by him believed in the worship of Lord Vishnu.
 
• His major literacy creations are the** ‘Kirtan Ghosa’**, ‘**Gunamala’** etc. The holy songs written by him are known as ‘**Borgeet’**
 
• The** dramas** written by him are known as** ‘Ankia Naat’** and **Sattriya Dance at that time was a part of it.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which among the following is incorrect pair of physical quantity and unit of measurement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pressure - Newton (N)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is measured in **Pascal (Pa)**, which is the **force per unit area.**

 
 
• **1 Pa** is **one newton per square meter (N/m2)**
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
 
 
• **Force **is measured in** Newton(N).**
 
• **Energy **is the capacity to do work and is measured in** joules (J)**.
 
• **Power **is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. It is measured in** watts (W)**.
 
• **Frequency **is the number of cycles per second and is measured in** hertz (Hz).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Some more physical quantities and their unit:**

questions.question: Who among the following found it more difficult to follow the rules of Jainism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peasants.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jainism **is a religion that emphasizes non-violence, self-control, and asceticism. It has strict rules and guidelines that its followers are expected to follow.
 
• Peasants, who were involved in agricultural activities and lived in rural areas, found it more difficult to follow the rules of Jainism due to the following reasons:
 
 
• Their livelihood depended on agriculture, which involved killing insects and animals. Jainism prohibits the killing of any living being, which made it difficult for peasants to follow this rule.
 
• **Peasants **had **limited resources and income**, **which made it difficult for them to follow the strict rules of Jainism**, **such **as **fasting **and **giving away wealth.**
 
• They had limited access to education and religious texts, which made it difficult for them to understand and follow the complex rules of Jainism.

• NRLM also focuses on building capacities and institutions of the rural poor to enable them to take charge of their own lives and livelihoods.
 
 
 
• It was **renamed** as** DAY-NRLM (Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Livelihoods Mission) **in **2015**.
 
• The program is supported partially by the **World Bank**.

questions.question: Humus, a dark colored amorphous substance is formed as a result of which process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humification.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humus **is a dark-colored, amorphous substance that is** formed due to the process of humification.**

 
 
• **Humification **is the process by which dead organic matter, such as leaves, twigs, and other plant and animal remains, are broken down by microorganisms and transformed into humus.
 
 
 
• It is an important component of soil, as it improves soil fertility, water retention, and nutrient availability.
 
• It is **a complex mixture of organic compounds**, including **humic acids**,** fulvic acids**, and **humin**.
 
 
• **Humic acids** are the most abundant and important component of humus, and they play a key role in soil fertility by improving soil structure, nutrient availability, and water retention.
 
• **Fulvic acids** are smaller and more soluble than humic acids, and they are involved in the transport of nutrients and other substances within the soil.
 
• **Humin** is a highly stable component of humus that is resistant to further decomposition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation **is the process by which large pieces of organic matter are broken down into smaller pieces, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Leaching **is the process by which water carries dissolved nutrients and other substances from the soil surface to deeper layers, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Mineralization **is the process by which microorganisms break down organic matter and release nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur into the soil to be easily available forms to plants.

questions.question: Who replaced Sanjay Kumar Verma as the Indian Ambassador to Japan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sibi George.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sibi George** is a 1993-batch Indian Foreign Service officer who is currently the **Ambassador of India to Japan.**
 
• He has previously served as India's Ambassador to Kuwait, Switzerland and the Holy See (Vatican City).
 
• In 2014, the Indian Government awarded him the S.K. Singh Award for Excellence in the Indian Foreign Service.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Baglay** is currently serving as **India's High Commissioner to Australia**.

 
 
• He has previously served as Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, been the Official Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs, and Joint Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office.
 
 
 
• **Sunil Arora** **was **the **23rd Chief Election Commissioner of India**.
 
 
• He also served as a secretary to the Government of India in two ministries.
 
 
 
• **Naveen Srivastava** is currently serving as **India's Ambassador to Nepal**.
 
 
• He has previously served as Ambassador of India to the Kingdom of Cambodia.
 
 
 
• **Sanjay Kumar Verma** is currently serving as India's Ambassador to Canada after serving as the Indian Ambassador to Japan.
